title: [Quiz] Review ways to measure your recommender.

cues.en: We've covered a lot in this section so far, but it's important to understand what makes a good recommender system before we start trying to build one.
cues.zh: 這一節目前介紹了很多內容，不過在開始建立推薦系統前，必須先了解什麼樣的推薦系統才算好。

cues.en: So, let's reinforce some of what we've learned with another short quiz.
cues.zh: 因此，再用一個簡短測驗，鞏固所學。

cues.en: Your first question is: which metric was used to evaluate the Netflix prize?
cues.zh: 第一個問題：Netflix Prize 使用哪個指標評估？

cues.en: By putting a one million dollar bounty on improving a specific metric, Netflix reshaped the world of recommender system research to focus on that metric, for better or worse, what was it?
cues.zh: Netflix 懸賞一百萬美元，獎勵改善某個特定指標，無論好壞，都改變了推薦系統研究的方向，讓大家聚焦於它。那是什麼指標？

cues.en: The answer is root mean squared error, or RMSE.
cues.zh: 答案是均方根誤差，簡稱 RMSE。

cues.en: But as we've said, accuracy isn't everything in the real world.
cues.zh: 但如同前面所說，在真實世界，準確程度不是一切。

cues.en: Users don't care how accurately you can predict how they rated movies they've already seen, they care about your ability to show them new things that they will love.
cues.zh: 使用者不在乎你能多準確預測他對已看過電影的評分，而是在乎你能否展示他會喜愛的新東西。

cues.en: Arguably, Netflix should have focused on a metric more focused on top-N recommendations, which leads to our next question:
cues.zh: 可以說，Netflix 應該聚焦於更著重 Top-N 推薦的指標，這就帶到下一個問題：

cues.en: What's a metric for top-N recommenders that accounts for the rank of the predicted items?
cues.zh: 哪個 Top-N 推薦指標，會考慮預測項目的排名？

cues.en: In truth, there's more than one, but there's only one that we talked about in this course so far.
cues.zh: 其實不只一個，但目前這門課只談過其中一個。

cues.en: The answer is average reciprocal hit rank, or ARHR for short.
cues.zh: 答案是平均倒數命中排名，簡稱 ARHR。

cues.en: It measures our ability to recommend items that actually appeared in a user's top-N highest rated movies, and gives more weight to these hits when they appear near the top of the top-N list.
cues.zh: 它衡量我們推薦的項目，是否實際出現在使用者評分最高的 Top-N 電影中；這些命中越接近推薦清單頂端，就給予越高權重。

cues.en: We talked about the long-tail and how there is real social value in recommending items that are relatively obscure, yet relevant to someone's unique, niche interests.
cues.zh: 我們談過長尾，也談過推薦相對冷門、卻符合個人獨特小眾興趣的項目，具有實際的社會價值。

cues.en: What metric tells us about how popular or obscure our recommendations are?
cues.zh: 哪個指標告訴我們，推薦有多熱門或多冷門？

cues.en: The answer is novelty, which is just a measure of the popularity rank of the items we recommend on the whole.
cues.zh: 答案是新穎性，也就是衡量推薦項目整體的熱門排名。

cues.en: And again, a balance must be struck between recommending popular items that establish trust in the recommender system, and more obscure items that may lead to serendipitous discovery from the users.
cues.zh: 再次強調，需要在熱門項目與較冷門項目之間取得平衡：前者建立對推薦系統的信任，後者可能讓使用者意外發現新事物。

cues.en: Which metric tells us whether we're recommending the same types of things all the time?
cues.zh: 哪個指標告訴我們，是否一直推薦相同類型的東西？

cues.en: For example, recommending every Star Wars movie because I watched one of them probably isn't a very serendipitous experience for the user.
cues.zh: 例如，只因為我看過一部《星際大戰》，就推薦每部《星際大戰》，對使用者而言，可能沒有多少意外發現。

cues.en: The answer is diversity, which is one minus the average similarity score between the items you recommend to each user.
cues.zh: 答案是多樣性，也就是一減去推薦給每位使用者的項目之間的平均相似度。

cues.en: And again, you need to be careful with this metric.
cues.zh: 同樣地，使用這個指標要小心。

cues.en: Never look at diversity alone, because you can get the highest diversity score by just recommending random stuff to people, and that's not a good recommender system.
cues.zh: 絕不能只看多樣性，因為隨機推薦東西，就能得到最高的多樣性分數，但那不是好的推薦系統。

cues.en: High diversity is often just a sign of bad recommendations.
cues.zh: 高多樣性往往只是推薦品質不佳的徵兆。

cues.en: Finally, which metric matters more than anything?
cues.zh: 最後，什麼指標最重要？

cues.en: It bears repeating!
cues.zh: 這值得再強調一次。

cues.en: That's the results of online a/b tests.
cues.zh: 就是線上 A/B 測試的結果。

cues.en: None of the offline metrics we discussed can take the place of measuring how real users react to the recommendations you put in front of them.
cues.zh: 我們討論過的任何離線指標，都無法取代衡量真實使用者，對眼前推薦的反應。

cues.en: You just can't simulate what goes on inside the heads of real people when they see new things, you have to try out your changes on them in the real world, and in a controlled manner, to see what works and what doesn't.
cues.zh: 你無法模擬真實使用者看到新東西時的內心活動，必須在真實世界，以受控的方式，對他們測試變更，才知道什麼有效、什麼無效。
